messages:
maya: heads up — observed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate after last kernel/runtime tweak on canary. small but consistent: ~62% -> ~19% on convo workloads. anyone else seeing this?
rahul: yep, noticed at 03:14 UTC. saw increased serialization size and more unique keys. perf dashboard snapshot: `prefix_hit_rate: 0.19, avg_latency_ms: +8`
simon: that was my kernel selection patch (align-pad to 8 bytes for some kernels). I changed serialization padding to reduce misaligned loads on a few GPUs.
maya: can you paste the exact serialization diff? curious if padding is injected into cache key bytes or just payload.
simon: quick example: original key bytes (hex) vs new: `...a1 b2 c3` -> `...a1 b2 c3 00 00` — padding appended to the prompt part during our proto->binary conversion. I think the cache key currently uses the raw serialized blob.
olivia: oof, that explains it. padding makes logically identical prompts look different. we should avoid raw-blob hashing.
rahul: I pulled a sample cohort. 120k requests where prompt text identical, but serialized keys had 3 variants due to padding/alignment and a trailing tool-fields order change. means warmup can't merge prefixes.
ci-bot: deploy: canary cluster s-3 completed kernel bump by simon at 03:05 UTC.
maya: mitigation ideas: (1) normalize serialization (strip padding) before hashing, (2) use canonicalized JSON for tool/function fields, (3) pin tokenizer/version into metadata not raw prompt bytes.
simon: agree. quick patch to strip trailing 0x00 from serialized prompt before keying is trivial. but need to be careful: some legitimately binary payloads might include 0x00.
rahul: alternative: compute key from canonical prompt + metadata tuple instead of raw proto. e.g. key = SHA(prefix_text_normalized + '|' + tokenizer_version + '|' + sorted_tool_fields). This avoids secrets of binary layout.
maya: I like that. also want to keep backward compatibility for existing cache entries. plan: implement canonical keying and keep old-key fallback for 72h while backfilling.
olivia: can we do a quick A/B test on canary? new keying logic on half of canary requests, old logic on the other half. measure hit-rate and latency.
simon: will open small PR with two things: (A) strip padding for immediate rollbackless improvement, (B) canonical key implementation behind flag for AB test.
rahul: profiler notes: kernel bump increases throughput but this key churn costs us in cold token generation and KV warmup. net perf is negative for conversational latencies. we should document in perf playbook: any change touching serialization requires a cachekey impact sign-off.
maya: agreed — adding a checklist item. action items: 1) simon to push strip-padding hotfix and flag PR (ETA 2h). 2) rahul to add AB experiment harness + metrics collection (hit-rate, avg_latency, warmup_tokens) (ETA 6h). 3) olivia to draft rollback playbook entry and compatibility window (ETA EOD).
simon: started PR: https://git.redwood/c/sim/kernel-serialize-fix — includes tests showing pad-trim improvement on sample.
rahul: I'll run a synthetic to validate: reproducer + script: ```bash
# repro diff keys
python tools/serialize_repro.py --sample 1000 --kernel bump
```
maya: thanks. if AB shows >10% hit-rate recovery we can promote to stable. and we should schedule a longer-term design to move key derivation away from raw protos. :thumbsup:
olivia: adding task to infra board: KEY-241 canonicalize-keying-spec + runbook.
ci-bot: issue created KEY-241 by olivia
maya: great. keep updates here and ping if you hit blockers. :sparkles:
